page: Amazon Web Services r7gd.16xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by 64 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 physical cores operating at 2.6 GHz on the ARM64 architecture. It features 512 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing capabilities, with Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 10% tier. Memory performance is a key strength, as demonstrated by a top-tier Passmark memory score and strong memory bandwidth results across both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks show strong performance, executing 101.36 million operations per second. However, single-core CPU performance and certain workloads, such as text generation on very small LLM models, show average to poor performance characteristics.

The ARM64 architecture and high resource density of the r7gd.16xlarge offer a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads compared to traditional x86 alternatives. The combination of high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage and substantial memory makes this instance well-suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data-intensive web serving. It is also appropriate for medium-scale LLM inference tasks and software compilation workloads.
